mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months indicates an extremely tight labor market, which elevates wage and input costs, compresses margins, and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5 percentage points in the same month signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases uncertainty and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies rise by >0.5% in the same month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of dual-decline episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 per month for five consecutive months, combined with an unemployment rate below 4%, signals a robust labor market expansion that boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 5 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase of at least 0.5% in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing recovery, which improves earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises by >0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained INDPRO expansion (t-test p > 0.10).
